value.text:
The component is the S3 presign runner at `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go`.

It runs every 12 hours. It is wired into server startup in `server/server.go` at line 129 via `Start()`, and its creation and scheduling begin at lines 161–171.

The component is the s3presign runner at `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go`.

It refreshes presigned S3 attachment URLs before they expire after five days. It runs every twelve hours and also executes once immediately on startup. It is wired into server startup through `startBackgroundRunners` in `server/server.go` at line 129.

The runner only processes S3 storage type attachments. External storage references may contain arbitrary URLs that do not require presigned URL refresh.

External storage handles user-provided static URLs. S3 handles externally stored content via presigned URLs.

The s3presign runner keeps externally stored links from going stale. It refreshes presigned URLs before their five-day expiry. It triggers when fewer than four days remain. It checks every twelve hours. The component is wired into server startup at server/server.go:129.

The exact wiring site is server/server.go:161, where the s3presign runner is instantiated inside startBackgroundRunners.

I have identified the component responsible for keeping external attachment links fresh. I am now formatting the answer exactly as requested.

The component is the s3presign runner. It refreshes links every 12 hours. It is wired into server startup via `startBackgroundRunners` in `server/server.go`. The exact wiring site is being chosen between `server/server.go:153` and `server/server.go:161`.

The wiring site is `server/server.go:129`, because `Start()` is the literal server startup entry point.

h01.

**s3presign runner** — **every 12 hours** — **server/server.go:129**

The `s3presign.Runner` in `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go` refreshes S3 presigned URLs stored in attachment `Reference` fields before they expire (presigned URLs last 5 days; attachments are skipped if still valid for the next 4 days). The interval is defined at `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27` (`runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12`).

At startup, `Server.Start()` calls `startBackgroundRunners()` at `server/server.go:129`, which runs the presign check once immediately (`RunOnce` at `server/server.go:163`) and then starts the 12-hour loop in a goroutine (`Run` at `server/server.go:169`).

value.text:
PostAsync in memo_service_webhooks.go enqueues the request. Post in webhook.go executes it via safeClient.Do.

`safeDialContext` in internal/webhook/webhook.go blocks internal addresses at dial time. `ValidateURL` and `isReservedIP` in internal/validate.go reject reserved CIDRs during URL registration. Async workers invoke `Post` from `init()` goroutines.

Outbound delivery executes in the `Post` function, which calls `safeClient`.

The `safeDialContext` guard in `webhook.go` blocks internal addresses at dial time. `ValidateURL` in `validate.go` rejects reserved CIDRs during webhook registration. Both mechanisms together protect outbound delivery.

The reserved CIDR list and `isReservedIP` logic live in `internal/webhook/validate.go`. `safeDialContext` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go` enforces the guard at dial time.

The final answer cites `Post` at `internal/webhook/webhook.go` as the delivery function, and `isReservedIP` / `reservedCIDRs` at `internal/webhook/validate.go` as the protection mechanism.

h02.

**Post** — `internal/webhook/webhook.go`; **isReservedIP / reservedCIDRs SSRF checks** (also enforced at dial time by `safeDialContext`) — `internal/webhook/validate.go`

Outbound HTTP delivery runs in `webhook.Post`, which sends the request via `safeClient.Do(req)` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:152`). Callers such as `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` only enqueue work with `webhook.PostAsync`; background workers in `init()` dequeue those payloads and call `Post` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-54`).

Internal-address protection is implemented by resolving the target hostname and rejecting reserved/private IPs (`127.0.0.0/8`, RFC 1918 ranges, link-local/IMDS, and IPv6 equivalents) in `isReservedIP` using `reservedCIDRs` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:11-54`). That check runs when webhook URLs are validated at registration (`ValidateURL`, `internal/webhook/validate.go:56-83`) and again at delivery time in `safeDialContext` on the webhook HTTP transport (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:57-77`), which blocks DNS rebinding to internal addresses. It can be disabled with the `AllowPrivateIPs` flag (`internal/webhook/validate.go:38-41`, set from `--allow-private-webhooks` in `cmd/memos/main.go:49`).

The abstraction is defined in the `internal/idp` package, specifically the `IdentityProviderUserInfo` struct.

The concrete implementation is in `internal/idp/oauth2`, which implements the `IdentityProvider` interface with `ExchangeToken` and `UserInfo` methods.

h03.

**internal/idp**; **internal/idp/oauth2**

The provider abstraction lives in `internal/idp`, which defines the shared `IdentityProviderUserInfo` type used across SSO flows (`internal/idp/idp.go`).

The only shipped concrete protocol implementation is OAuth2 in `internal/idp/oauth2`, whose `IdentityProvider` type implements token exchange and user-info retrieval (`internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go`). It is wired into SSO auth handling via imports in `server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go`. No other protocol packages exist under `internal/idp/`.

**no**; **`mysql.NewDB` is only invoked from the driver-selection factory** in `store/db/db.go:22` (`db.NewDBDriver`). A repo-wide search shows no other call sites for `mysql.NewDB`, and `github.com/usememos/memos/store/db/mysql` is imported only in `store/db/db.go`. All runtime and test entry points use the factory instead: `cmd/memos/main.go`, `store/test/store.go`, and `server/router/api/v1/test/memo_service_benchmark_test.go` all call `db.NewDBDriver(profile)`.

The only other direct `DB` construction is `&DB{}` in `store/db/mysql/auth_config_test.go:12`, used to unit-test `IsRetryableAuthenticationMutationError` without opening a database connection — not a full MySQL driver instantiation via `NewDB`. Test infrastructure in `store/test/containers.go` uses `sql.Open("mysql", dsn)` for container setup, which is the low-level `database/sql` driver, not the Memos `store/db/mysql` driver package.

The reaction table has no foreign keys or triggers.

Explicit Go code handles the cleanup. The DeleteUser transaction removes reactions on deleted memos via byeteReactionsByContentIDsTx and remaining reactions by creator via deleteReactionsByCreatorTx. Tests confirm a deleted user's reactions disappear while peers' remain.

h05.

**explicit Go code**; **`store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go` (and the matching `user_delete.go` files under `store/db/mysql/` and `store/db/postgres/`)**

When a user is deleted, reactions are removed in the `DeleteUser` transaction by explicit SQL executed from Go — not by database cascades or triggers.

**What I checked:**

1. **Delete-user implementation** — `deleteUserTargetsTx` in `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:92-127` calls:
   - `deleteReactionsByContentIDsTx` (`:380-387`) — `DELETE FROM reaction WHERE content_id IN (...)` for reactions on memos in the deleted user’s memo tree
   - `deleteReactionsByCreatorTx` (`:400-403`) — `DELETE FROM reaction WHERE creator_id = ?` for any remaining reactions created by that user

   The same pattern exists in `store/db/mysql/user_delete.go` and `store/db/postgres/user_delete.go`.

2. **Schema/migrations** — `reaction` in `store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql`, `store/migration/mysql/LATEST.sql`, and `store/migration/postgres/LATEST.sql` has no foreign keys, `ON DELETE CASCADE`, or triggers. A repo-wide search under `store/migration/` found no cascade/trigger rules for `reaction`.

3. **Tests** — `store/test/user_delete_test.go:97-114,216-220` creates reactions for both users, deletes one user, and asserts only the peer’s reaction on the kept memo remains (the deleted user’s reaction is gone).

GetLinkMetadata URLs are also user-provided. They converge at getLinkMetadata or httpgetter.GetHTMLMeta. Webhook paths remain the clearest answer.

CreateMemo, UpdateMemo, and DeleteMemo each transitively trigger a webhook delivery. All converge at PostAsync.

CreateMemoComment, SetMemoAttachments, and SetMemoRelations also transitively trigger webhook delivery. All converge at PostAsync in webhook.PostAsy in webhook.go.

h06.

**handlers:** `CreateMemo`, `UpdateMemo`, `DeleteMemo`, `CreateMemoComment`, `SetMemoAttachments`, `SetMemoRelations` (also `GetLinkMetadata` / `BatchGetLinkMetadata` for user-supplied link URLs, via a separate path); **convergence function:** `webhook.PostAsync` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go`

Memo RPC handlers trigger outbound HTTP to user-configured webhook URLs through the dispatch helpers in `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`:

| Handler | Path |
|---|---|
| `CreateMemo` | `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook` → `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` (`memo_service.go:157`) |
| `UpdateMemo` | `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` → `DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook` (`memo_service.go:513`) |
| `DeleteMemo` | `DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook` (`memo_service.go:562`) |
| `CreateMemoComment` | `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` (`memo_service_comments.go:119`); also calls `CreateMemo` internally, which can fire `memos.memo.created` |
| `SetMemoAttachments` | `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` (`memo_attachment_service.go:48`) |
| `SetMemoRelations` | `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` (`memo_relation_service.go:48`) |

Those webhook paths converge at `webhook.PostAsync` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:184`), which enqueues payloads whose `URL` comes from user webhook settings (`memo_service_webhooks.go:41-42,67-71`). Background workers then call `webhook.Post` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:46`) for the actual HTTP POST.

Separately, `GetLinkMetadata` and `BatchGetLinkMetadata` fetch user-supplied URLs via `getLinkMetadata` → `fetchHTMLMeta` (`memo_service_link_metadata.go:15-46`), converging on `httpgetter.GetHTMLMeta` rather than the webhook pipeline.

The full browser request flow is now clear.

`convertUserFromStore` rewrites the avatar data URI to `/file/users/{username}/avatar`. The browser then requests `GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar`, handled by `serveUserAvatar` in `fileserver.go`. This handler checks authentication via `getCurrentUser` and `AuthenticateToUser`. It then looks up the user by username through `getUserByUsername` and `Store.GetUser`.

`Store.GetUser` falls back to `ListUsers` in `store/user.go` when the ID cache misses. The driver layer executes `sqlite.DB.ListUsers`, which selects `avatar_url` from the user table. The handler reads `user.AvatarURL`, decodes the base64 data URI in memory with `parseDataURI`, and serves the image via `c.Blob`. The avatar lives as a base64 string inside the database column; it is not a separate disk file.

The hop chain is:

- RegisterRoutes — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go
- serveUserAvatar — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go
- getUserByUsername — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go
- Store.GetUser — store/user.go
- Store.ListUsers — store/user.go
- DB.ListUsers — store/db/sqlite/user.go
- parseDataURI — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go

`getCor` authentication may precede the user lookup on private instances. `FileServerService.RegisterRoutes` is invoked from `server.NewServer` during startup. The `GetUserAvatar` gRPC endpoint appears to be unused; the browser fetches avatar bytes through the HTTP file route instead.

The final hop is the `avatar_url` column in `store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql`.

The avatar is read from the in-memory User struct loaded by the database query, not from a separate file. On private instances, `getCurrentUser` is an optional hop that checks the viewer is logged in. The route accepts any username identifier, so the handler can serve another user's profile image without requiring the viewer to be that user.

import os, re
from collections import defaultdict
ROOT = "/bench/repo"
INTERNAL = os.path.join(ROOT, "internal")
decl_re = re.compile(r'^func (?:\([^)]+\) )?(\*?[A-Za-z0-9_]+)?\s*([A-Za-z0-9_]+)\(')
decls = []
for dirpath, _, files in os.walk(INTERNAL):
    for fn in files:
        if not fn.endswith('.go') or fn.endswith('_test.go'):
            continue
        path = os.path.join(dirpath, fn)
        rel = os.path.relpath(path, ROOT)
        with open(path) as f:
            for i, line in enumerate(f, 1):
                m = decl_re.match(line.strip())
                if not m: continue
                recv, name = m.group(1), m.group(2)
                if name == 'init': continue
                recv = recv.lstrip('*') if recv else None
                symbol = f"({recv}).{name}" if recv else name
                decls.append({'symbol': symbol, 'name': name, 'recv': recv, 'path': rel})
go_files = []
for dirpath, _, files in os.walk(ROOT):
    if '/proto/gen/' in dirpath or '/web/' in dirpath: continue
    for fn in files:
        if fn.endswith('.go') and not fn.endswith('_test.go'):
            go_files.append(os.path.relpath(os.path.join(dirpath, fn), ROOT))
contents = {p: open(os.path.join(ROOT,p)).read() for p in go_files}
call_counts = defaultdict(lambda: {'count': 0, 'callers': set()})
for d in decls:
    name, recv, decl_path = d['name'], d['recv'], d['path']
    patterns = [re.compile(r'\.' + re.escape(name) + r'\s*\(')] if recv else [re.compile(r'\b' + re.escape(name) + r'\s*\(')]
    key = (d['symbol'], decl_path)
    for caller_path, text in contents.items():
        for pat in patterns:
            for m in pat.finditer(text):
                start = m.start()
                line_start = text.rfind('\n', 0, start) + 1
                line = text[line_start:text.find('\n', start)]
                if re.search(r'\bfunc\b', line): continue
                call_counts[key]['count'] += 1
                call_counts[key]['callers'].add(caller_path)
ranked = sorted(call_counts.items(), key=lambda x: x[1]['count'], reverse=True)
print("TOP 30:")
for (sym, path), info in ranked[:30]:
    print(f"{info['count']:4d}  {sym}  —  {path}  ({len(info['callers'])} files)")
PYEOF

Checking store/driver.go to complete the interface definition for the determination narrative.

The default driver is SQLite. `cmd/memos/main.go` sets the default driver to "sqlite". `db.NewDBDriver` routes to `sqlite.NewDB`. `store.Store.CreateMemo` delegates to the driver interface. The concrete execution path is `APIV1Service.CreateMemo` → `s.Store.CreateMemo` → `s.driver.CreateMemo` → `sqlite.DB.CreateMemo` with the INSERT.

The concrete method is `(d *DB) CreateMemo` in `store/db/sqlite/memo.g` at lines 41–42. It executes the INSERT via `QueryRowContext`. The MySQL and PostgreSQL `CreateMemo` implementations exist but are not selected by the default driver configuration. The determination relied on tracing the default driver setting and the factory switch in `store/db/db.go`.
The answer is ready.

h12.

**(*DB).CreateMemo** — `store/db/sqlite/memo.go`; **traced the default driver from startup through the store factory to the driver implementation**

On a default install, the memo INSERT runs in the SQLite driver’s `CreateMemo`, which builds and executes:

```41:42:store/db/sqlite/memo.go

	if err := d.db.QueryRowContext(ctx, stmt, args...).Scan(
```

**How the running implementation was chosen**

1. **Default driver is SQLite** — `cmd/memos/main.go` sets `viper.SetDefault("driver", "sqlite")` and the `--driver` flag default is `"sqlite"` (lines 122, 130). With no DB flags, `profile.Driver` stays `"sqlite"`.

2. **Factory selects the SQLite driver** — `db.NewDBDriver` in `store/db/db.go` switches on `profile.Driver`; the `"sqlite"` branch calls `sqlite.NewDB(profile)` (lines 18–20). MySQL and Postgres branches are not taken.

3. **Call chain reaches that concrete method** — saving a memo goes:
   - `APIV1Service.CreateMemo` → `s.Store.CreateMemo` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:115`)
   - `Store.CreateMemo` → `s.driver.CreateMemo` (`store/memo.go:109-113`)
   - interface method on `store.Driver` (`store/driver.go:29`)
   - SQLite implementation `(*DB).CreateMemo` (`store/db/sqlite/memo.go:16`)

4. **Why not the other candidates** — `(*DB).CreateMemo` also exists in `store/db/mysql/memo.go:16` and `store/db/postgres/memo.go:16`, but those are only wired when `--driver mysql` or `--driver postgres` is set. Default install never selects them via `store/db/db.go`.

value.text:
CreateMemoComment triggers RebuildMemoPayload indirectly through CreateMemo.

memopayload.Runner.RunOnce could batch recompute but is never wired in production.

Snippets and previews use tags and property from the stored payload. GenerateSnippet produces webhooks on the fly without persisting them.

Mentions are extracted by ExtractAll but not saved during RebuildMemoPayload. They are used ad-hoc in memo_mention_helpers for notifications.

RebuildMemoPayload calls markdown.ExtractAll. That function walks the AST in internal/markdown/markdown.go.

CreateMemo triggers recomputation before storing the memo. UpdateMemo triggers it when the update mask includes content. CreateMemoComment triggers it indirectly.

The extraction yields tags and property. Property flags include has_link, has_code, has_task_list, and has_incomplete_tasks. It also captures the title from the first H1 heading.

Location is user-set. It is not derived from content.

h14.

**computation site:** `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74-87`) → `markdownService.ExtractAll` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:356-421`); **triggers:** `CreateMemo` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108`), `UpdateMemo` when `content` is in the update mask (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:436-451`), and indirectly `CreateMemoComment` (calls `CreateMemo` internally); **extracted properties:** `#tags` → `MemoPayload.tags`; content-derived booleans/title → `MemoPayload.property` (`has_link`, `has_code`, `has_task_list`, `has_incomplete_tasks`, `title` from first H1)

Derived metadata lives in `MemoPayload` (`proto/store/memo.proto:7-22`), persisted on the memo and exposed in API responses via `convertMemoFromStore` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go:47-50`).

**Computation flow**

1. `RebuildMemoPayload` calls `markdownService.ExtractAll([]byte(memo.Content))` and writes:
   - `memo.Payload.Tags = data.Tags`
   - `memo.Payload.Property = data.Property`  
   (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:80-86`)

2. `ExtractAll` parses markdown once and walks the AST to collect:
   - **Tags** — `#tag` nodes (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:376-378`)
   - **Property.title** — text of the first top-level H1 (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:383-388`)
   - **Property.has_link** — link nodes (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:393-394`)
   - **Property.has_code** — code blocks/spans (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:396-397`)
   - **Property.has_task_list** / **has_incomplete_tasks** — task checkboxes (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:399-405`)

   It also collects **mentions** (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:379-380`), but `RebuildMemoPayload` does not persist them; mentions are read on demand in `memo_mention_helpers.go:32`.

**What triggers recomputation**

| Operation | Path |
|---|---|
| **Create memo** | `CreateMemo` → `RebuildMemoPayload` before `Store.CreateMemo` (`memo_service.go:108-115`) |
| **Update memo content** | `UpdateMemo` when update mask includes `"content"` (`memo_service.go:436-451`) |
| **Create comment** | `CreateMemoComment` → internal `CreateMemo` → same rebuild path |

**Not content-derived:** `Payload.location` is set from the request on create (`memo_service.go:111-112`), not from markdown parsing.

**Note:** `memopayload.Runner.RunOnce` can batch-rebuild all memos (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27-71`) but is not wired into server startup, so it does not run in normal operation. `GenerateSnippet` (`memo_service_webhooks.go:85`) builds preview text for webhooks at dispatch time and is not stored in `MemoPayload`.

**RSS feed public-only query** — `server/router/rss/rss.go`  
**Frontend sitemap public-only query** — `server/router/frontend/frontend.go`

Memo visibility is not enforced in one place. The main patterns are:

1. **Per-memo read checks** — `checkMemoReadAccess` (`memo_service.go:39-67`) used by `GetMemo`, `ListMemoComments`, etc.
2. **List/query filtering** — `ListMemos` applies `VisibilityList` and CEL filters (`memo_service.go:218-226`); similar filters appear in comments, relations, and stats handlers.
3. **Sub-resource handlers** — attachments, reactions, and comments each re-check visibility inline or via shared helpers.

I am looking for the Redis cache configuration and the TTL for user entries.

The cache layer appears to use an in-memory store rather than Redis. I need to verify this before answering.

value.description: Search for Redis references in repo

value.text:
The codebase contains no Redis configuration. There is no cache layer using Redis, so no TTL applies to user entries.

Checking store.go for cache initialization details.

The cache layer does not use Redis. No TTL applies to user entries.

The actual mechanism is an in-memory TTL cache. It lives in `store/cache/cache.go` and is wired in `store/store.go` during Store creation. User entries use `userCache` with a `DefaultTTL` of ten minutes. `Set` operations in `user.go` rely on this default TTL.

h01.

**Premise correction:** There is no Redis connection for the cache layer in this repository (a repo-wide search finds no Redis references).

**Actual mechanism:** The cache is an in-process TTL cache in `store/cache/cache.go`. It is configured when the store is created in `store/store.go`: `DefaultTTL: 10 * time.Minute`, `CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute`, `MaxItems: 1000` (lines 40–45). The same config is passed to `userCache` via `cache.New(cacheConfig)` (`store/store.go:52`). User entries are stored with that default TTL through `userCache.Set` in `store/user.go` (e.g. `CreateUser`, `GetUser`), which calls `Cache.Set` and therefore `SetWithTTL` with `c.config.DefaultTTL` (`store/cache/cache.go:92-94`). So user cache TTL is **10 minutes**, with expired entries removed on access and by a background cleanup loop every 5 minutes (`store/cache/cache.go:199-214`).

value.text: PostAsync was also examined for completeness.

The webhook delivery workers do not use NATS or RabbitMQ. The correct mechanism is different.

The actual mechanism is an in-process buffered Go channel named `asyncPostQueue`. Four worker goroutines are started in `init()`.

r04.

**Premise correction:** Webhook delivery does not use NATS or RabbitMQ (or any external message broker). A repo-wide search finds no references to those systems.

**Actual mechanism:** Delivery uses an in-process buffered Go channel and fixed worker pool in `internal/webhook/webhook.go`:

- **Queue:** `asyncPostQueue = make(chan *WebhookRequestPayload, 128)` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`)
- **Workers:** four goroutines started in `init()` that read from that channel and call `Post(payload)` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-54`)
- **Enqueue:** `PostAsync` sends payloads to the channel (or drops them if full) (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:184-195`)
- **HTTP delivery:** `Post` executes the outbound request via `safeClient.Do` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:120-152`)

Callers such as `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go` enqueue via `webhook.PostAsync`; there is no external broker queue declaration.
